findings.title: Parent walk dereferences Parent in loop post statement
findings.message: The loop post statement calls p.Parent.AsTree() before the nil check in the body can stop iteration. The body breaks when p.Parent == nil only after the earlier branch runs, so the post statement is not reached then; however, if the handler ever continues past the root (e.g. the first branch does not match), the break precedes it and is fine. The real risk is p.Parent being a non-nil interface holding a typed nil, which would panic in AsTree. Walking the parents is also repeated on every hover event for every control, which is wasteful.
findings.suggestion: Write the loop as `for p := widget.AsTree(); p != nil; { ...; if p.Parent == nil { break }; p = p.Parent.AsTree() }` to make the nil handling explicit.
findings.evidence: for p := widget.AsTree(); p != nil; p = p.Parent.AsTree() {

findings.title: Property set after capture may leak
findings.message: The property is compared with == on an interface holding *toolbarDragGesture. That is fine for pointers. However, SetProperty is called after CapturePointer succeeds, so if a capture ends synchronously between them the property would be left stale; the end() cleanup only runs when b.active is set, and the property is set after b.active, so a stale entry could persist if end() ran in between.
findings.suggestion: Set the property before CapturePointer and delete it on the error path, or make the guard check b.active.
